Particle arrays and examples¶

Design and public interfaces¶

Each material has a writable float64 structure of arrays, accessed through L.materials[p]. Materials share one grid. The coordinator deposits every material before combining periodic endpoints, identifying occupied nodes, and normalising mass-weighted fields.

Linear neighbours are bottom-left, bottom-right, top-right, top-left. Quadratic neighbours are a tensor-product nine-entry stencil, with boundary/periodic mapping described in numerical methods. Particle and grid vectors retain three components; geometry and transport remain two dimensional. Constitutive tensor traces and norms reduce tensor axes only.

Particles(P, G, material, material_id) constructs one batch. ParticleSystem(P, G) coordinates the material list. Supported laws implement law(particles, material_parameters, simulation_parameters) and update history and dstress. Updated mechanics uses neo-Hookean elastic stress, objective rate-form plasticity, and algebraic fluid stress; it evolves F, J, V, and rho. The optional mechanics='legacy' compatibility configuration uses fixed volume and incremental constitutive integration. Rigid materials bypass deformation/stress evolution and follow prescribed velocity. See the numerical methods and constitutive models. The registry in constit.py is the only material dispatch mechanism.

Uniform mass/volume properties, velocities, and grain fractions are copied into independent writable arrays. Initial velocity must be (3,) or (n, 3); composition must be (ns,) or (n, ns). Initial fractions must be nonnegative and sum to one. PHI, when provided, takes precedence over phi. Coordinates must have exactly n entries. Density, volume, and grain sizes must be positive and finite. A zero-particle material is valid.

The grid stores pressure, gammadot, mu, I, eta, and other constitutive diagnostics as mass-weighted sums. Call G.physical(name) to divide once by nodal mass. G.phi, G.s_bar, G.pk, and G.shear_rate are already physical fields. G.shear_rate is the bulk velocity-gradient measure; deposited gammadot is a material constitutive diagnostic. Empty-node quotients contribute zero. G.segregation_m, G.segregation_phim, and G.segregation_phi hold the deformable transport inventory separately from rigid material. G.segregation_particle_dphi stages the bounded species-aware increments for the next composition update.

Periodic left/right grid endpoints duplicate one physical node. Sum unique columns (array.reshape(ny, nx, ...)[:, :-1]) when measuring periodic totals. Merge deposited sums once per stage; do not add periodic endpoints a second time. Particle positions wrap with modulo arithmetic before cell lookup.

Timestep and input interfaces¶

The timestep uses a strain-before-force order:

  1. Reset grid, update loading, determine cells and basis functions.

  2. Deposit mass, momentum, composition, and kinetic pressure across all materials.

  3. Merge periodic sums, calculate valid nodes, and impose momentum constraints.

  4. Gather velocity, update deformation/volume/density and strain/history/stress, and deposit diagnostics. Legacy mode omits deformation/volume evolution.

  5. Deposit forces, impose force boundaries, and update grid momentum.

  6. Calculate bulk shear rate and, if enabled, conservative segregation exchanges.

  7. Return species-aware composition exchanges, then update particle position and velocity and handle particle boundaries.

Particle mass remains fixed during deformable motion; updated volume is J*V0 and physical density is m/V. Legacy mode alone fixes volume and reconstructs particle density from nodal occupancy.

Input conventions:

  • A single material object or list in P.S.

  • segregate_grid as an alias for segregate; contradictory explicit values fail.

  • Uniform initial_v, or per-particle initial velocities.

  • Pressure initialisation modes, steady viscous/Pouliquen flow, and the steady Poiseuille formula within its steady regime.

  • Boundary flags, default output flags, output filenames, and particle-data column order (x, y, grain fractions).

  • Inlet placement and cadence use material geometry. Only materials declaring inlet_rate enter through an enabled inlet. Injection properties must be uniform per material; each new batch gets freshly initialised constitutive history.

Outlets remove all persistent fields together. Inlets append full batches. Scratch connectivity is rebuilt after either operation, and material counts follow the actual array lengths. Prescribed per-particle rigid velocities travel with their rows through removal.

Callbacks are at_start(L, P, G), after_every_timestep(L, P, G), after_every_savetime(L, P, G), and at_end(L, P, G). after_ever_timestep is a compatibility alias. A custom callback replaces the corresponding default stage; it is responsible for any desired plotting, energy recording, or saving at that stage. Default energy histories grow with actual steps, so dynamic timesteps do not overflow preallocated buffers.

run stops at the requested final time, shortening the last step when needed. Dynamic timestep selection considers all materials and ignores inactive zero-speed or zero-segregation-rate limits. Invalid resulting timesteps fail explicitly. run(..., output=False) suppresses every output callback.

Numerical conventions¶

Repeated node indices accumulate all particle contributions. Cell lookup uses floor, validates positions, and assigns exact upper edges to the final cell. Periodic coordinates wrap before lookup; node validity is determined after all materials deposit and periodic sums are merged. Internal forces contract the Cauchy stress with spatial shape gradients and current particle volume.

Pressure-dependent flow laws use compression-positive confinement. At zero pressure, the undefined inertial-number diagnostic is stored as zero; Pouliquen friction uses its high-inertial-number limit when the shear rate is nonzero. At zero shear rate, effective viscosity follows the selected model’s cap or Newtonian limit. See constitutive models.

Segregation conserves mobile species inventories using local equal-mass exchanges. G.gammadot and the constitutive fields remain distinct from the bulk-grid shear rate. The diffusion coefficient has an explicit zero-inertial- number convention; very small nonzero inertial numbers can still make it sensitive. See segregation transport.

Runtime and dependency baseline¶

The supported baseline is Python 3.14, pinned to 3.14.10 in .python-version. Dependency floors are NumPy 2.5.4, SciPy 1.18.1, Astropy 8.0.2, Matplotlib 3.11.2, and pytest 9.2. The complete resolved environment is recorded in uv.lock. Use uv sync --extra dev --locked with a current uv release to reproduce it. The regression suite runs on Python 3.14. Benchmark reports record their own environment and source fingerprints; use measurements matching the configuration you intend to run.

Validation and remaining limitations¶

Tests cover shape functions, affine flow, pure rotation, repeated-node transfers, unequal particle properties, body/internal forces, constitutive histories, pressure and flow initialisation, multiple materials, empty batches, domain boundaries, periodic seams, inlets/outlets, dynamic timestep selection, callbacks, saved array shapes, and readable nonempty figures. The complete ball run and 100-/1,000-step bidisperse/three-class/eight-class segregation runs are included.

Kernel reference comparisons use rtol=1e-10, atol=1e-12; short trajectories use rtol=1e-8, atol=1e-12. Tests run with runtime warnings treated as errors.

Segregation checks measure species masses, local fraction sums, bounds, and pure- layer mixing without clipping or normalisation. Run python -m benchmarks.segregation_drift to reproduce the conservation report. The normalise_phi compatibility option is unnecessary for the conservative operator and can conceal an invalid configuration.

Materials share a momentum grid: this does not provide separate-body contact or independent material velocity fields. Traction scaling uses the first material’s uniform reference density. The numerical methods describe diagnostics and the verification suite; unsupported registry names fail explicitly rather than selecting a different law.

The user manual builds the current reStructuredText and Markdown sources together. See documentation maintenance for build instructions and the checked-in HTML layout.
